sentences.en: Figuring out what makes a terrorist tick is not easy, and law enforcement and counterterrorism officials have been turning more and more to psychologists to try to do just that.
sentences.zh: 要弄清楚是什么让恐怖分子产生动机并不容易，执法部门和反恐官员正越来越多地求助于心理学家来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: In this episode,
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，

sentences.en: we talk with a psychologist who has spoken face-to-face with former members of violent extremist organizations in an effort to understand how and why people become involved in terrorism,
sentences.zh: 我们采访了一位心理学家，他曾与暴力极端组织的成员面对面交谈，试图了解人们是如何以及为何卷入恐怖主义的，

sentences.en: as well as why some choose to walk away.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么有些人选择退出。

sentences.en: John Horgan is professor of security studies at the School of Criminology and Justice Studies at the University of Massachusetts Lowell,
sentences.zh: 约翰·霍根（John Horgan）是马萨诸塞大学洛厄尔分校犯罪学与司法研究学院的安全研究教授，

sentences.en: where he's also the director of the Center for Terrorism and Security Studies.
sentences.zh: 他同时也是该校恐怖主义与安全研究中心的主任。

sentences.en: His research focuses on terrorist behavior.
sentences.zh: 他的研究重点是恐怖分子的行为。

sentences.en: He has more than 70 publications on terrorism and political violence.
sentences.zh: 他在恐怖主义和政治暴力领域发表了70多篇著作。

sentences.en: He's interviewed hundreds of terrorists around the world.
sentences.zh: 他采访过世界各地数百名恐怖分子。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Horgan.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，霍根博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: I guess the most common question is, are there certain characteristics or a profile of the type of person who is most likely to become a terrorist?
sentences.zh: 我想最常见的问题是，是否存在某种特征或画像，能描述最有可能成为恐怖分子的人？

sentences.en: No is the short answer.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是：没有。

sentences.en: It hasn't stopped us from looking for such a profile, but four decades of psychological research on who becomes a terrorist and why hasn't yet produced any profile.
sentences.zh: 这并没有阻止我们寻找这样的画像，但四十年来关于谁会成为恐怖分子及其原因的心理学研究，至今尚未得出任何画像。

sentences.en: If there is no simple way to profile who might be a terrorist, how do you begin to understand and study terrorist behavior?
sentences.zh: 如果没有简单的方法来描绘谁可能是恐怖分子，那么你如何开始理解和研究恐怖分子的行为呢？

sentences.en: Oh, very slowly and with a great deal of patience.
sentences.zh: 哦，非常缓慢，而且需要极大的耐心。

sentences.en: We've discovered in recent years that it is possible for us to reach out to and identify individuals who have disengaged from terrorism.
sentences.zh: 近年来我们发现，我们有可能接触并识别那些已经脱离恐怖主义的人。

sentences.en: So we can actually ask questions to people who were once involved in high-profile terrorist activity.
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际上可以向那些曾经参与过高调恐怖活动的人提问。

sentences.en: So we can conduct research.
sentences.zh: 因此我们可以进行研究。

sentences.en: We can conduct research systematically, and we can try to answer questions about who becomes involved in terrorism and why.
sentences.zh: 我们可以系统地进行研究，并尝试回答关于谁会卷入恐怖主义以及原因的问题。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say that we are at the very, very early stages in terms of developing a science of terrorist behavior.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，在发展恐怖分子行为科学方面，我们还处于非常、非常早期的阶段。

sentences.en: Psychology as a discipline hasn't yet contributed very, very much to the study of terrorism.
sentences.zh: 心理学作为一门学科，对恐怖主义研究的贡献还非常、非常有限。

sentences.en: So we've got a long, long way to go.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还有很长、很长的路要走。

sentences.en: In the case of the Boston Marathon bombings, was there anything about that attack that you thought was unique in terms of the psychological impact or the response and, you know,
sentences.zh: 就波士顿马拉松爆炸案而言，你认为那次袭击在心理影响或反应方面有什么独特之处，而且，你知道，

sentences.en: just about the attackers themselves?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是关于袭击者本身？

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say that there are still quite a number of unanswered questions surrounding the Boston Marathon bombings, questions around the perpetrators,
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，围绕波士顿马拉松爆炸案仍有许多悬而未决的问题，关于肇事者的问题，

sentences.en: their likely motivations.
sentences.zh: 以及他们可能的动机。

sentences.en: I think what struck me as being particularly concerning in the wake of the Boston Marathon bombings was the fact that our resilience seems to have taken quite a substantial hit.
sentences.zh: 我认为在波士顿马拉松爆炸案之后，让我感到特别担忧的是，我们的韧性似乎受到了相当大的打击。

sentences.en: And this idea that, for example, that this kind of threat essentially posed an existential challenge to security and a national security in the United States, I think,
sentences.zh: 而且这种观点，例如，这种威胁本质上对美国的安全和国家安全构成了生存挑战，我认为，

sentences.en: really contributed to the idea that this is very, very much something that was overblown, really.
sentences.zh: 真的助长了一种观点，即这在很大程度上是被夸大了。

sentences.en: So I think there are some pretty serious questions we're going to have to ask about our ability to bounce back from these kinds of attacks.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，关于我们从这类袭击中恢复过来的能力，我们必须提出一些非常严肃的问题。

sentences.en: The more we learn about the nature of the attack, the more we learn about the preparations for it, the more we're finding out that this attack, in all likelihood,
sentences.zh: 我们对袭击的性质了解得越多，对袭击准备工作的了解就越多，我们就越发现这次袭击，极有可能，

sentences.en: couldn't possibly have been prevented.
sentences.zh: 是不可能被阻止的。

sentences.en: And there was very, very, very little leakage, very, very, very little initial signals that could have alerted people to what these individuals were all about.
sentences.zh: 而且几乎没有泄露任何信息，几乎没有任何最初的信号可以提醒人们这些人到底想干什么。

sentences.en: And that is a certain, it indicates, at least to me, a certain level of risk that we're going to have to live with.
sentences.zh: 这表明，至少对我来说，这是一种我们必须忍受的特定风险水平。

sentences.en: You've interviewed hundreds of terrorists.
sentences.zh: 你采访过数百名恐怖分子。

sentences.en: How forthcoming do you think they are in these interviews?
sentences.zh: 你认为他们在这些采访中有多坦诚？

sentences.en: Surprisingly, they are forthcoming.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，他们很坦诚。

sentences.en: I've interviewed about 150 terrorists since about 1995, and we know that approaches can be made.
sentences.zh: 自1995年左右以来，我采访了大约150名恐怖分子，我们知道是可以接触到他们的。

sentences.en: They tend to be cooperative.
sentences.zh: 他们往往很配合。

sentences.en: They tend to be facilitative, but only insofar as they see us as academics as possibly a tool for propaganda.
sentences.zh: 他们往往很乐于提供帮助，但前提是他们将我们这些学者视为可能的宣传工具。

sentences.en: There's very often an agenda.
sentences.zh: 他们通常有自己的议程。

sentences.en: Sometimes they want to use us to push a message out there.
sentences.zh: 有时他们想利用我们来传播某种信息。

sentences.en: In some cases, where we've been very, very fortunate to speak to disengaged terrorists,
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，我们非常有幸能与脱离恐怖主义的人交谈，

sentences.en: they are very willing to talk about their experiences because they want to say how they've changed.
sentences.zh: 他们非常愿意谈论自己的经历，因为他们想说出自己是如何改变的。

sentences.en: They want to say that, they want to be able to talk to us about why the dangers exist for young people becoming involved in terrorism nowadays.
sentences.zh: 他们想说，他们想和我们谈谈为什么现在年轻人卷入恐怖主义的危险依然存在。

sentences.en: So they want to talk to us.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想和我们谈谈。

sentences.en: How difficult, and you mentioned this, disengaging, how difficult is it for terrorists to disengage, so to speak?
sentences.zh: 你提到了脱离，恐怖分子脱离（所谓的）有多困难？

sentences.en: Are there programs?
sentences.zh: 有相关的项目吗？

sentences.en: How do they go about that?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何做到的？

sentences.en: Well, when we started this research a number of years ago, we began with the assumption that once a terrorist, always a terroriSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，几年前我们开始这项研究时，我们假设：一日为恐怖分子，终身为恐怖分子。

sentences.en: That once you're in, you're in, and there really is no way out except, in the words of one former terrorist, feet firSt.
sentences.zh: 一旦你进去了，就出不来了，用一位前恐怖分子的话说，除非是“横着出来”。

sentences.en: That's now not the case.
sentences.zh: 现在情况并非如此。

sentences.en: We know that just as there is a steady stream of people who become involved in terrorism, there's also a fairly steady and regular stream of people who disengage.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，正如有一股源源不断的人卷入恐怖主义一样，也有一股相当稳定和规律的人群正在脱离。

sentences.en: It's not as difficult as we would have once imagined for people to actually leave, and people leave for a gamut of reasons.
sentences.zh: 人们离开并没有我们曾经想象的那么困难，而且人们离开的原因多种多样。

sentences.en: There is a variety of push and pull factors that contribute to that, and this is what our current research is trying to uncover.
sentences.zh: 有各种各样的推动和拉动因素促成了这一点，这正是我们目前的研究试图揭示的内容。

sentences.en: We found, in particular, we found that disillusionment plays a very, very significant role in individuals' decisions, rather, to want to leave behind terrorism.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，特别是我们发现幻灭感在个人决定想要抛弃恐怖主义的过程中起着非常、非常重要的作用。

sentences.en: Are there de-radicalization programs out there?
sentences.zh: 现在有去激进化项目吗？

sentences.en: There certainly are many de-radicalization programs out there.
sentences.zh: 当然有很多去激进化项目。

sentences.en: We've started to see the emergence of these programs around about 2003, 2004, and now, I mean, they've really proliferated.
sentences.zh: 我们大约在2003年、2004年开始看到这些项目的出现，现在，我的意思是，它们确实激增了。

sentences.en: I've spent a lot of time in Pakistan this year.
sentences.zh: 今年我在巴基斯坦花了很多时间。

sentences.en: In fact, I've spent time looking at many of these de-radicalization prograMs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我花时间研究了许多这些去激进化项目。

sentences.en: Some are more effective than others.
sentences.zh: 有些比其他的更有效。

sentences.en: Some of the work we're doing in Pakistan right now is about understanding how individuals who have been detained for terrorist offenses
sentences.zh: 我们目前在巴基斯坦所做的一些工作，是关于了解那些因恐怖主义罪行而被拘留的人，

sentences.en: can effectively be rehabilitated and reintegrated back into the communities that they once claimed to act on behalf of.
sentences.zh: 如何才能有效地进行康复，并重新融入他们曾经声称为其行事的社区。

sentences.en: Is there a way to identify potential terrorists and to prevent them from engaging in terrorism?
sentences.zh: 有没有办法识别潜在的恐怖分子并阻止他们参与恐怖主义？

sentences.en: I think it's becoming very, very difficult to identify potential terrorists.
sentences.zh: 我认为识别潜在的恐怖分子正变得非常、非常困难。

sentences.en: In recent years, we've had a very emotional and a very, I suppose, engaging conversation about who becomes a terrorist and why.
sentences.zh: 近年来，我们就谁会成为恐怖分子以及原因进行了一场非常情绪化，而且我想说，非常引人入胜的对话。

sentences.en: And that discussion has been rooted in this concept of radicalization.
sentences.zh: 而那场讨论植根于激进化这个概念。

sentences.en: And one of the assumptions in that has been that people become radicalized.
sentences.zh: 其中一个假设是人们会被激进化。

sentences.en: They get exposed to certain kinds of thoughts, certain kinds of ideas.
sentences.zh: 他们接触到某种思想，某种观念。

sentences.en: And that then somehow puts them at greater risk for involvement in terrorism.
sentences.zh: 然后这在某种程度上使他们卷入恐怖主义的风险增加。

sentences.en: The more evidence we're finding, particularly from firsthand interviews with former terrorists,
sentences.zh: 我们发现的证据越多，特别是来自对前恐怖分子的第一手采访，

sentences.en: is that that logic may not necessarily hold in very, very many cases, as intuitive as it might seem.
sentences.zh: 就越表明这种逻辑在很多情况下未必成立，尽管它看起来很直观。

sentences.en: So we're finding right now that the initial concept of radicalization isn't as helpful as we once thought.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在发现，最初的激进化概念并不像我们曾经认为的那样有帮助。

sentences.en: And certainly we need to go back to basics with respect to much of the research here.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们需要回归基础，重新审视这里的大部分研究。

sentences.en: And this is where I implore more and more psychologists to step up and engage with the kinds of theories, the kinds of methodological frameworks that we have at our disposal
sentences.zh: 这就是我恳求越来越多的心理学家站出来，运用我们现有的各种理论和方法框架的原因，

sentences.en: to really cut beyond a lot of the otherwise very woolly thinking in this area.
sentences.zh: 以真正超越该领域许多模糊不清的思维。

sentences.en: Well, thank you, Dr. Horgan.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你，霍根博士。

sentences.en: This has been very interesting.
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣。

sentences.en: Thanks for joining us.
sentences.zh: 感谢你加入我们。

sentences.en: It's my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: For more information and links to Dr. Horgan's work with the Center for Terrorism and Security Studies at UMass Lowell, please visit our website at speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息及霍根博士在马萨诸塞大学洛厄尔分校恐怖主义与安全研究中心的工作链接，请访问我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton with the American Psychological Association's Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是美国心理学会《心理学谈话》节目的奥黛丽·汉密尔顿（Audrey Hamilton）。
